status: Documentation audit complete; physical sound-chain qualification not performed
user_request: Verify that the recommended equipment can carry out the complete planned experiment.
scope: Current work is sound generation, delivery and measurement. Neural recording/decoding integration remains deferred.

user_clarifications.initial_stage: Quick checkout in the mouse setup, followed by transfer of the audio equipment to sheep.
user_clarifications.initial_speaker_distance: Not decided yet, explicitly reported by Howard.
user_clarifications.later_stage: Primary Rice sheep measurements remain planned; sedation is a Rice adaptation from the awake, alert SONIC sheep.
user_clarifications.calibration_geometry: Calibrate at the mouse ear/reference position first, then independently at the sheep ear/reference position. Reuse hardware, not the old geometry-specific correction.

conclusion: Manufacturer specifications support a plausible compatible sound chain. No documented fatal 32 kHz fundamental or 10 ms digital-timing mismatch was found. MR3 output at the required level/geometry and actual short-pip behavior remain unverified, so the complete sound experiment cannot be certified from this audit.

paper_requirements.presentation_level: Approximately 80 dB SPL at sheep-ear distance; neither a mouse prescription nor a confirmed Rice setting.
paper_requirements.unresolved: Exact initial 37-frequency array, acoustic geometry, level convention and numerical acoustic timing/level tolerances are not supplied.

evidence_matrix.check: M50/iD4 or iD14 power and input loading
evidence_matrix.evidence: M50 requires nominal 24-48 V at 10 mA and load >=600 ohms; interfaces specify 48 V +/-4 V at 10 mA/channel and 2.8 kohm mic input.

evidence_matrix.status: Supported by component specifications; delivered calibration still to inspect
evidence_matrix.evidence: M50 is specified 3 Hz-50 kHz with individual chart/ECF. Interface preamp at minimum gain and ADC/DAC extend to 40 kHz. Actual fixed-gain response, serial correction file coverage and uncertainty are not measured.

evidence_matrix.status: Exact sample arithmetic verified, hardware fidelity unverified
evidence_matrix.evidence: At 96 kSa/s: 960 samples/pip, 192 samples per 2 ms ramp, 576 samples between ramps. Nyquist is 48 kHz, above the 32 kHz fundamental. Continuous precomputed playback avoids per-pip OS scheduling. A host buffer longer than 10 ms does not itself prevent the sequence.

evidence_matrix.status: Credible budget candidate; actual required SPL unverified
evidence_matrix.evidence: Official response illustration shows 32 kHz near its midband level, but distance, drive, settings and uncertainty are absent. The 92.5 dB peak-at-1-m claim is not a 32 kHz output guarantee.

Manual specifies power with DRC on but no compression attack/release or bypass guarantee. Original Erin measurements extend to about 20 kHz and use long sweeps/multitone tests. They do not establish 32 kHz, 10 ms envelopes. Fixed delay longer than 10 ms does not itself prevent 100 pips/s.

evidence_matrix.status: Documented 1 kHz reference; full chain not physically calibrated
evidence_matrix.evidence: R8090 supplies 94/114 dB at 1 kHz, stated +/-0.5 dB. Included M50 ADP1 nominally matches its half-inch port. Seal and before/after repeatability require checks. This is separate from the microphone frequency correction.

evidence_matrix.status: Manufacturer supports Mac; exact host remains untested
evidence_matrix.evidence: A read-only inventory of this workstation found no Audient audio interface enumerated. Analog microphone/speaker presence cannot be determined from that inventory. This workstation reports macOS 27.0.1; the retrieved vendor OS list does not explicitly list that version. This is an unresolved qualification item, not evidence of incompatibility, and the eventual experiment Mac may differ.

evidence_matrix.status: iD14 revision enables a stronger test; actual channel matching and timing unverified
evidence_matrix.evidence: iD4 has only one full-band mic/line input. Its instrument input can potentially carry a characterized lower-band marker but is not a specified full-band reference or TTL input. iD14 permits simultaneous microphone and full-band electrical-reference capture.
Paper-style blocks imply 80-150 seconds each and about 16-30 minutes for 12 blocks. No full-duration duplex test or future neural marker/clock interface has been implemented or tested.

revised_recommendation.adoption_status: M50 is user-selected. iD14 is a new recommendation for stronger bench verification; not a reported purchase or a claim of user adoption.
revised_recommendation.change: Replace iD4 MKII with iD14 MKII and add one HSS-005 TRS cable. Retain M50, R8090, MR3 candidate, XLR cable and microphone stand.
revised_recommendation.reason: Capture actual acoustic output and an electrical reference simultaneously. The iD4 remains viable for the original acoustic-only checkout; this revision is not a finding that it cannot play the sequence.

reference_connections: Duplicate the waveform on output 2 -> balanced TRS -> rear line input 2, phantom off, minimum gain
M50 -> rear XLR mic input 1, phantom on
Record both inputs simultaneously at native 96 kSa/s; mute direct/software input monitoring
revised_recommendation.reference_limits: Characterize the relative DAC output and ADC input gain/delay first. Output 2 is a duplicate electrical reference, not automatically an exact measurement of output 1. Output +12 dBu is below line-input +21 dBu maximum at minimum gain. No TTL or neural clock alignment is added.

required_physical_checks: Define mouse reference position/distance, stimulus alphabet, level convention and numerical pass tolerances with the lab. Do not inherit the sheep exposure setting as a mouse prescription.
Inspect delivered M50 serial chart/ECF through 32 kHz; check calibrator adapter seal, stand fit, USB power and exact host native 96 kSa/s duplex operation.

Fix interface/speaker gains and settings; characterize response and relative channel delay. Record reference calibration before and after testing. Prefer the 94 dB calibrator setting and verify headroom; 114 dB may clip at a gain used for 80 dB stimuli.

At the fixed ear/reference position, measure all retained frequencies, particularly 27/32 kHz, for target level, available headroom, clipping, spectral contamination within the measurable band and level compression.

Record actual continuous 10 ms sequences with 2 ms end ramps, including repeats and large low/high jumps. Assess duration, spacing, frequency-dependent delay, residual energy into the following pip, level consistency and missed events.

Repeat for the intended complete run, using 80-150 second blocks and a minimum 12-block duration when reproducing the paper block schedule; inspect underruns, stream discontinuities, drift and startup/idle behavior.
Use wired TRS, documented Monitor/neutral EQ settings and firmware, and disable standby as documented. Do not claim DRC has been bypassed.
Repeat acoustic calibration and sequence checks after transferring the hardware to the sheep geometry. Design neural timing/clock alignment separately before that portion of the experiment.
measurement_limits: The 96 kSa/s adaptation is not bit-for-bit replication of the paper's 192 kSa/s DAC.
The M50/96 kSa/s capture cannot measure the 64 kHz second harmonic of 32 kHz; this is not complete ultrasonic THD qualification.
Microphone magnitude correction and a 1 kHz level reference do not alone verify speaker phase/transient behavior or neural responses.
actions: Research, read-only local audio inventory and nominal calculations only. No purchase, supplier outreach, software installation, audio output, physical calibration or animal experiment occurred.

nominal_level_calculation.scope: Calculated nominal 1 kHz headroom, not a physical or 32 kHz measurement
nominal_level_calculation.assumptions: M50 typical34mV/Pa; preampgain30dB; +12dBu interface inputfullscale atminimumgain; actual serialsensitivity/gain may differ.
nominal_level_calculation.implication: Check levels and prefer the94dB calibrator setting; 114dB may clip at a gain chosen for80dB stimuli. Do not change gain between reference calibration and stimulus recording without recalibrating.
